newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIA-INVEKS BROKERAGE CONFIRMS EYES BOURSE.
newsitem.headline: LATVIA-INVEKS BROKERAGE CONFIRMS EYES BOURSE.

text.p: Latvian Inveks brokerage, which has been bought by Estonia's Hoiupank, on Monday said it will continue with plans of intensifying its activity on the market and become a bourse member.
"We plan to work more intensively with the new controlling stake owner in place," Jevgeny Bogdanov, executive manager of Inveks, told Reuters.
"Inveks will become a member of the cental depository next week, at the latest during this month, and then buy shares in the bourse," Bogdanov said.
"Inveks could be considered as one of the leaders of the free market and we ended last year with a profit," he added.
Inveks was formed in 1995 by two companies dealing in vouchers and two people and its share capital is 40,240 lats.
"We have the capital in Latvian T-bills," Bogdanov said.
He said the sale came after a competition of several Estonian banks, which was won by Hoiupank.
"We saw an increased interest from Estonia late last year and especially at the beginning of 1997," Bogdanov said.
